subject: Recap: Renewal & expansion call — Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmecorp.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Renewal & expansion call — Acme Corp

Jordan / Alicia — thanks again for your time on the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same view:

Summary of discussion:
- Renewal window: current contract expires Jan 31, 2027. You indicated procurement typically needs ~8-10 weeks for approvals.
- Current usage: steady growth in embedding and chat workloads; spikes during end-of-quarter reporting drove higher latency on peak loads.
- Pain points: (1) token costs on frequent embedding calls, (2) tail latency during spikes for live chat, (3) lack of predictable throughput for batch processing jobs.
- New workloads: planning to add vector search for knowledge base (Q1 2027) and real-time chat for customer support (pilot in Dec).

Recommended path (what we discussed):
1) Add Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity to guarantee throughput and reduce tail latency.
2) Adopt Redwood Optimize for batching/cache suggestions and quantization guidance to bring per-token cost down on embeddings.
3) Start a canary for the real-time chat workload on a dedicated pool (2-3 week pilot) before broad rollout.

Action items / owners:
- Redwood (Marissa): share Q2 usage report and two pricing options (mixed reserved vs. burstable) - attached.
- Redwood (Monica): provide SOC 2 summary + security/compliance FAQ and sample contract redlines link.
- Acme (Jordan): confirm procurement timeline and any internal procurement contacts; share any additional security evidence required.
- Acme (Alicia): confirm target date for vector search pilot (tentative: early Jan).

Proposed next touchpoints:
- Week of Nov 9: follow-up on procurement timeline and pricing questions.
- Nov 16: 30-min technical canary plan with your infra and our runtime team if you want to proceed.

Attachments:
- Q2-usage-report.csv (high level usage + cost breakdown)
- redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (pricing options and tier comparisons)

If I've missed anything, please flag. Happy to adjust next steps based on your procurement cadence.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement timeline: we aim to have approvals completed by mid-Jan 2027. Legal will want to run through SOC 2 + data handling specifics; I expect a couple of back-and-forths.
- Pilot scope: for the chat canary, we want to validate 95th percentile latency at peak load and verify behavior under session state (KV cache) eviction.
- Pricing: the dedicated vs burstable comparison looks helpful. Can you include an estimate for expected monthly cost delta if we commit to a 12-month reserved pool sized for our current QPS + 30%?

Also: please send the SOC 2 summary and any relevant network architecture docs we should circulate internally. Alicia and I will sync with procurement and share a primary procurement contact by Fri Nov 6.

Next steps for us:
- Jordan: provide procurement contact (ETA Nov 6)
- Acme infra: will prepare service-level requirements for the canary

Thanks - Jordan
